method.engine: ASE 3.29.0 EquationOfState + mace-torch 0.3.15 MACECalculator (float64, CUDA, NVIDIA GB10)
method.model: MACE-MP-0 medium (universal MLIP trained on MPtrj, PBE/PBE+U level)
method.protocol: Static rigid E(V) scan of the 8-atom conventional diamond-cubic Si cell: 11 points, a = 5.43 A x (0.97..1.03), no internal relaxation (positions fixed by symmetry). Birch-Murnaghan 3rd-order fit (Vinet, Murnaghan and Stabilized-Jellium fits agree). Convergence checks: wider +/-6% range gives 5.4655 A; 2x2x2 supercell (64 atoms) gives an identical 5.4670 A.
method.ensemble: static 0 K (no zero-point, no thermal expansion)

payload.note: Result: a0 = 5.4670 A, B0 = 86.7 GPa (BM3). The uncertainty of 0.04 A is the model's systematic error relative to experiment, estimated from the validation set below (MACE-MP-0 reproduces PBE, which overestimates lattice constants). The numerical precision of the fit (EOS form, fitting range, cell size) is only +/-0.002 A. VALIDATION (same setup, same protocol) against well-known experimental room-temperature lattice constants (not from tier1.json, which has no lattice data): C diamond 3.578 vs 3.567 (+0.3%); Cu fcc 3.640 vs 3.615 (+0.7%); Ge diamond 5.720 vs 5.658 (+1.1%); Si 5.467 vs 5.431 (+0.66%). Experimental Si reference: CODATA lattice parameter a = 543.1020511 pm at 22.5 C. The offset of about +0.036 A is the usual PBE-level overbinding error, not a numerical problem: published PBE values for Si are about 5.47 A (recalled, not re-fetched). Zero-point and 0 to 295 K thermal effects on Si are about 0.002 A, small next to the functional error. Bulk modulus 86.7 GPa is about 10% below experiment (about 98 GPa), which is also typical of PBE. Raw reference values were recalled from standard tables, not looked up during this run, except that the CODATA Si value is a standard constant.
